claim_policy: Every deck claim must cite a repo source path, live economics Sheet, or explicit assumption. Null beats confidently wrong; no route/city IDs invented in deck copy.

sections.positioning: Start where Yassir is sourced and Atlas is already grounded: Tunisia and Morocco. Algeria now has source-backed route mint candidates, but remains held until exact Atlas geometry and economics gates pass.

partner_context.their_ambition: Yassir is the leading super app for French-speaking Africa and the Maghreb. YC and Google Cloud both describe a platform operating in 45 cities across Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia, with ride-hailing, last-mile delivery, and financial services as the connective tissue.
partner_context.their_pressure: Ride-hailing density compounds in the cities, but coastal North Africa leaves trips fragmented between taxis, ferries, rail, and informal transfers. The premium-water surface is still unclaimed.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is a branded water tier inside Yassir: app-booked, cashless, multimodal, captain-operated, and sequenced from short proven urban/coastal legs before any longer Quanta-LR roadmap routes.
partner_context.algeria_note: Yassir is Algeria-originated; Algeria is now explicitly prioritized as the next home-market unlock, but held from map/economics until exact Atlas geometry and country-reference data exist.

hero.title: Yassir × Navier — the Maghreb super-app, now with a water tier
hero.subtitle: Start where Yassir is sourced and Atlas is already grounded: Tunisia and Morocco. Algeria now has source-backed route mint candidates, but remains held until exact Atlas geometry and economics gates pass.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Yassir-branded premium water mobility tier across existing Atlas coastal Maghreb markets: Tunis/La Goulette/Sidi Bou Said/Djerba, then Tangier/Casablanca/Rabat/Agadir/Al Hoceima. The app owns the customer, wallet, driver-partner/captain supply, and door-to-pier leg; Navier owns the efficient hydrofoiling vessel and operating playbook.

sections.why_now: North African cities are building super-app behavior while coastal trips remain slow, cash-heavy, and disconnected from the daily mobility stack. The first partner to connect ride-hail, port pickup, water transfer, and arrival ride in one checkout becomes the default premium layer for coastal trips.
sections.multimodal_fit: Yassir can book the whole journey: home pickup → marina/port handoff → Navier water leg → arrival taxi/food/cash/payment touchpoints. This is not a ferry brochure; it is a super-app surface extension.
proof_points: YC profile: Yassir operates in 45 cities across Algeria, Morocco, and Tunisia and offers ride-hailing/last-mile delivery/financial services.
Google Cloud customer story repeats the 45-city Algeria/Morocco/Tunisia operating footprint and frames Yassir as a Maghreb super-app.
Official Yassir site foregrounds ride-hailing, food delivery, market, cash, and driver/delivery partner onboarding.
Existing Atlas geometry already has Tunisia and Morocco coastal nodes; Algeria has no supported Atlas city in this repo pass, so it is held.
Algeria is explicitly source-backed via Yassir Algeria, Yassir Express city selector, Google Cloud, and YC; it is held only because Atlas geometry/economics gates are not yet met.
Algeria route source hardening batch 1 now identifies Algiers Bay, Béjaïa–Alger, and Oran–Mostaganem mint candidates; all remain held until exact Atlas IDs are sealed.

objections.objection: Yassir is not proven city-by-city on every route.
objections.response: Correct; this pass uses country-supported inheritance only into existing Atlas markets and labels the evidence tier. Exact city support can promote later, but it is not required to show grounded Atlas markets.

objections.objection: Algeria is Yassir's home market — why not include it on the map?
objections.response: Because this repo pass has no Algeria Atlas city/boarding-point geometry. It gets a priority gap ticket, not a fake dot.

objections.objection: Some Morocco/Tunisia demand rows are estimated.
objections.response: The economics publish grounded floor separately from estimated upside; the model and proposal expose that separation.

objections.objection: Can N30 do the longer Mediterranean legs?
objections.response: No. The proposal range-gates them to Quanta-LR roadmap or review; long legs are not faked.

objections.objection: Why is Algeria not shown as a Yassir market if Yassir started there?
objections.response: It is now addressed as the first-class home-market mint queue. Current Atlas data has no Algeria city/boarding-point IDs and no Algeria country-reference row, so displaying or modeling it now would violate exactness-over-coverage.

growth.anchor_note: LB-254: M_today = transport_spend_pool_yr (demand x fare); the ladder's capture = floor/pool (the capture that actually built the floor: ~0.90 captive / ~0.10 contested / blended). Replaces the legacy floor/0.10 divisor that inflated captive markets ~9x.

_whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
_whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.

alpha_density._doc: avg greenfield corridor demand / avg sourced corridor demand. Sourced = cherry-picked best; greenfield thinner.

_census._note: tier1 market-making (island-hop/regional/inter-city/trunk) + tier2 cluster-spokes; Japan/Ryukyu carved out; local intra-hub micro-segments excluded.

greenfield._doc: WIDTH lever. SAM_sourced_only = depth on the sourced corridors (no greenfield). SAM/TAM/network/platform = full addressable network (sourced + greenfield). SOM floor is unaffected (it is the sourced corridors).
